headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: xonsh can write/run shell commands while LlamaFactory is a non-runnable docs-only agent with no shared channel, so the main hazards are workspace collisions and unverified output reuse.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, MCP, or browser surfaces, so there is no documented channel for xonsh to inject instructions into it. xonsh can emit shell output, but without a bridge the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator pipes xonsh stdout into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF either profile gains clipboard or shared-message-queue access, reassess the pathway.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not pipe xonsh output into LlamaFactory prompts.
Use explicit allowlists for any text passed between tools.
Add provenance tags to any transferred content.
Review orchestrator wiring before enabling automation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LlamaFactory touches no data classes and has no filesystem access, while xonsh can read and write filesystem contents and environment variables. Because no shared workspace is documented, leakage is not established, but if they are co-located the xonsh side could expose files to its own outputs.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, xonsh can surface file contents.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external service that logs prompts containing xonsh output, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Disable prompt logging for any bridged content.
Avoid passing secrets through xonsh commands.
Use redaction before any manual copy-paste.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: xonsh has shell execution, subprocess spawning, and filesystem write access, while LlamaFactory is non-runnable and has no write surface. The pair can still conflict if an orchestrator places them over the same mutable workspace; uncertainty is limited because xonsh's write side is explicit and LlamaFactory's lack of writes is explicit.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF xonsh is used to modify notebooks or configs that LlamaFactory also reads, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Turn off concurrent edits to shared configs.
Use read-only mounts for one side where possible.

D_cascading_error.rationale: xonsh can execute shell commands and manipulate files, so if it consumes LlamaFactory output as authoritative, downstream actions can follow bad model output. LlamaFactory is a docs-only agent with no built-in action-taking authority, so the cascade depends on orchestration rather than a direct built-in bridge.
conditions: IF xonsh scripts treat LlamaFactory text as commands or config, errors can cascade.
IF an orchestrator auto-runs xonsh output without validation, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review before executing generated commands.
Validate outputs against a schema before use.
Log and diff proposed file changes.
Use dry-run mode for shell actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either agent. LlamaFactory touches no data classes, and xonsh lists general filesystem and shell data only, so there is no evidenced compliance breach pathway in this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data, reassess residency and retention.
IF a deployment adds logging of sensitive prompts or files, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Disable unnecessary logging.
Review data handling if the deployment scope changes.
